releases.summary: The Health page shows live system status, the app starts about a third faster after an update, addresses that can't be links get a quick answer, and the daily click summary arrives at 08:00.

sections.title: Notifications
items: The daily click summary arrives at 08:00 Croatian time instead of 01:15. It still covers yesterday. The weekly summary stays on Monday at 09:00.

sections.title: Performance
items: The app starts about a third faster after an update, so the gap while hrva.cc restarts is shorter.

An address that can't be a link, such as /.env, /wp-login.php or /config.php.bak, gets the small "This link doesn't exist" page right away, without a database lookup. Links saved with letters outside A to Z open as before.
The public health check no longer waits for the mail server.
Every response has a Server-Timing header with the time the server spent on it.

sections.title: Admin
items: The Health page shows live system status and refreshes every 30 seconds. At the top, one line lists anything that is wrong, in plain sentences. Below it are traffic and response times for the last 60 minutes, the database and Redis (up or down, response time), email (when the last one was sent, failures in the last 24 hours), screenshots and VirusTotal (today's use against the daily limit, the queue, and pauses longer than 5 minutes), blocklists (lists that are out of date), the server (version, uptime, startup time, memory) and the last run and outcome of each scheduled job. When the database is down, the page says so.

/actuator/prometheus serves Prometheus metrics, only with the header Authorization: Bearer <APP_METRICS_TOKEN>. A wrong or missing token gets 401. Without APP_METRICS_TOKEN set on the server the endpoint doesn't exist and answers 404, for admins too.
New settings for self-hosters: APP_METRICS_TOKEN, and APP_INSPECTION_BROWSER_SECONDS_DAILY_LIMIT, the Browser Run seconds per day the Health page compares today's use with (600 by default).

releases.summary: Screenshots, redirect chains and VirusTotal verdicts for links in the review queue, the warning page on links without an account while they wait for review, a plain-text part in every email, and a round of fixes.

sections.title: Link Safety
items: A link made without an account that the checks flag, or that a visitor reports, shows the warning page while its review is open, with the note "hrva.cc is checking this link. Continue only if this is the address you expected." The page goes away when the review is closed, whatever the outcome. A warning page the link has because its site is new or its name looks machine-made stays. The help page on links without an account says so.
Making an identical link without an account while one is in review gives you that link, with its warning page, instead of a new one.

When a link you make without an account goes to review as it is made, the note under the new link reads "This link is being checked. People who open it see its address first until the check is done." instead of the note about a new site.

sections.title: Emails
items: Every email has a plain-text part as well as the HTML, with the full address behind every link and button.
When an app connected to your account sent you to an address with letters outside A to Z, the email about it also gives the plain spelling, such as xn--okolada-i6a.hr.

sections.title: Performance
items: Links stay in the redirect cache for 24 hours instead of one, so repeat visits are answered without the database for longer. A changed, turned off or deleted link leaves the cache right after the change is saved, and again 2 seconds later. When the cache can't be reached, removing the link is tried again 30 seconds later and then 5 minutes after that.

sections.title: Privacy
items: When a link enters the review queue, its destination changes while it's in review, or an admin takes a screenshot from Inspect, Cloudflare receives the link's destination address to take the screenshot. When a link enters the review queue, its destination changes while it's in review, or an admin uses Look up on VirusTotal, VirusTotal receives a fingerprint (SHA-256) of the address, never the address itself. Only an admin's Send to VirusTotal sends the address, and VirusTotal then shows it to its paying users. The privacy page says so.

sections.title: Admin
items: Each link that enters the review queue gets a screenshot: Cloudflare Browser Run opens the link's destination at phone size. The nightly cleanup deletes a screenshot once it's 7 days old. The queue shows it in a new column. Select it, or Inspect, to open it with the page's title and status.

Inspect, in the review queue and on All URLs, has Take screenshot, or Take again once there is one. A screenshot an admin asks for is taken even when the link is blocked. One the queue asked for is not taken when the link was blocked first.

Screenshots pause until midnight UTC when the day's Browser Run time is used up, for as long as Cloudflare asks when it limits requests, and for an hour when Cloudflare refuses the API token. The link stays queued, and Inspect says why.

Each link that enters the review queue is looked up on VirusTotal by the SHA-256 fingerprint of its address, so only a report VirusTotal already has can match. The destination is looked up first, then the same address with a slash after a bare host name, then where its redirects end, then that address with the slash. The lookup waits for the link's redirect check, for up to 2 minutes, so it knows where the redirects end. Inspect shows how many scanners flag it and links to the report.

When VirusTotal has no report, Send to VirusTotal in Inspect sends the address to be scanned, after a confirmation that VirusTotal then shows the link to its paying users. The verdict is looked up a minute later, first by the id VirusTotal gave the scanned address, then by the fingerprints. Every send is in the audit log.

Look up on VirusTotal in Inspect starts a new lookup by fingerprint. It sends VirusTotal only the fingerprint, never the address, so it can retry a lookup that failed or found no report without publishing the link.

VirusTotal lookups make at most one call every 15 seconds and stop at a daily cap, 480 by default, until midnight UTC. When VirusTotal doesn't answer, answers with an error or limits requests, the lookup keeps waiting and tries again a minute later. A refused API key pauses lookups for an hour.
When the owner changes the destination of a link in review, the link gets a new screenshot and a new VirusTotal lookup. An admin's change still closes the review.
Every hop of a link's redirect chain is kept in full, and Inspect lists them under Where it goes. A link checked before this release shows its chain after its next redirect check.

Site settings has three new switches under Safety, all on by default: "Warning page while a link without an account waits for review", under the warning page switch, "Screenshots of links in review" and "VirusTotal lookups for links in review". The last two do nothing, and say so, until CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_BROWSER_API_TOKEN, or VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY, are set on the server.
A review closed with Looks fine that removed the warning page says warningPage: cleared in the audit log.
The link cache hit ratio on Stats › System and the Health page counts only redirects of links that exist.
Owner and Created in the review queue are their own columns only where the table has room beside the screenshot, and show inside the Short link cell otherwise.

sections.title: API
items: GET /api/v1/admin/urls/{urlId}/inspection answers a link's redirect chain, screenshot state and VirusTotal verdict. GET /api/v1/admin/urls/{urlId}/inspection/screenshot answers the image, POST /api/v1/admin/urls/{urlId}/inspection/screenshot queues a new one and answers 202, POST /api/v1/admin/urls/{urlId}/inspection/virustotal sends the link to VirusTotal, and POST /api/v1/admin/urls/{urlId}/inspection/virustotal/lookup starts a new lookup by fingerprint and answers 202. All five are for admins.
Review queue entries have redirectChain, screenshot and virusTotal.
Link responses have warningPageForReview: true while the warning page shows because the link waits for review, and left out otherwise.

sections.title: Fixes
items: A "Reconnecting…" notice shows at the top of the page while hrva.cc restarts, and goes away once it answers.

Password managers no longer take the custom domain name box on Settings, or the box for asking for more domains, for a sign-in code field. The name box was why Proton Pass still offered a two-step code there.

A build that hangs stops after 30 minutes instead of running for up to 6 hours, a hung test run stops after 20, and Redis host names are looked up with Java's own resolver, which removes a cause of those hangs.

releases.summary: Use a removed custom domain again, analytics breakdowns across all your links, emails and chat messages that name hrva.cc and say what happened, and a round of fixes.

sections.title: Custom Domains
items: A custom domain you removed stays on the Custom domains card in Settings for 30 days, in a closed Removed domains section, newest first. Select Use again next to it to add the domain as a new one, with no links on it.
A domain you removed yourself after it was active is set up again without a review. A check that flags the domain, or no room for new domains right now, still sends it to review.

A domain goes back to review, as when you first applied, when an admin removed it, when an admin or a blocklist rule turned it off before you removed it, when it never became active, when its name is international (an xn-- name), when an admin block rule matches its name, or when your account has been flagged as a possible scammer. A name the link check blocks is refused with "This domain can't be used on hrva.cc." The card says before you select Use again whether the domain is reviewed again.

Use again isn't offered when another domain, yours or someone else's, holds the name, and the removed domain then shows with no button. While Cloudflare is still removing a domain, the card says to check back in a few minutes.

A domain you use again counts toward your domain limit and toward the 5 applications a day, like any other application. At the limit, Use again is refused until you remove or withdraw another domain. Removed domains don't count.
Domains removed before this release are treated the same way: one hrva.cc turned off and you then removed, and one an admin removed, go back to review.

Admin Domains no longer lists removed domains with the others. They are in a closed Removed domains section, newest removal first, and can be sorted by when they were removed. Domains removed without a recorded date come last.

sections.title: Analytics
items: The analytics overview breaks clicks down across all your links, for the range you pick: QR scans and other clicks, referrers, countries, devices, browsers and operating systems. Each list shows the 10 with the most clicks and adds the rest together as Other. The Statistics help page explains it.

sections.title: Emails
items: Emails come from "hrva.cc" instead of a bare address.

Email subjects changed to name hrva.cc and say what happened, so a mail filter on an old subject stops matching. The new subjects are Reset your hrva.cc password, Verify your email for hrva.cc, Your hrva.cc account was deactivated, Your hrva.cc account will be deactivated on 29 November 2026, Someone tried to sign up to hrva.cc with your email, A passkey was added to your hrva.cc account, Your link was blocked as unsafe, and Your link hrva.cc/abc expires on 3 November 2026.
"Best regards" is removed from every email. Each one greets you with Hi and your email address, and says "blocked" for a blocked link.
The email about a link blocked as unsafe names the flagged address instead of "malware".
The expiry email shows the date and time in UTC, and its button opens your dashboard.
The inactivity warning gives the time without use in whole years when it is a whole number of years, and the new-sign-up email to admins says what the account signed up with.
The email asking you to verify your address says verify throughout.
The decisions email to admins is sent when a possible scammer is waiting.

sections.title: Notifications
items: A Discord channel you add shows a destination that is an IP address, or a name that looks like an email address, as it is, like the other channel types.
The daily summary lists up to 20 links and then says "and N more", counting the links left out.
ntfy messages with a title that has a non-ASCII character, such as the dash in the weekly summary, now arrive.

Titles and wording were made consistent: hrva.cc: 1 of your links looks broken, hrva.cc: your week of 19–25 October 2026, and a test message that reads "This channel works" followed by the channel's name.

The webhook bodies for the daily and weekly summaries gain moreLinks, moreDeadLinks and moreEndingSoon, the number of links left out of a list. No existing field changed. The /help/notifications page now describes the body of every event.

sections.title: Link Safety
items: The addresses Google Safe Browsing flagged for a blocked link are never cut off. Whole addresses are kept, and an address too long to keep is shown as its host. This holds for links blocked after a redirect too.

sections.title: Security
items: An authenticator entry you add from now on is labelled "hrva.cc" instead of "hrva.cc Url Shortener". Entries you added earlier keep their label, and their codes keep working.

sections.title: Admin
items: The sidebar badges count only their own queue: Review counts links and bio pages, and Domains counts domain applications and limit requests.
Every audit log row names what it acted on: the domain and its owner, the account, or the link and its destination. A limit request shows the old and new limit.
A link on a custom domain is named by that domain in audit rows.
Admin Discord alerts say "no account" for a link made without one, and write a domain rule's reason after a colon.

sections.title: API
items: POST /api/v1/users/me/domains/{id}/use-again uses a removed custom domain again and answers 201 with the new domain. Custom domain responses have a useAgain field: SKIPS_REVIEW, NEEDS_REVIEW or CLOUDFLARE_REMOVAL_PENDING on a removed domain, and null on any other domain, when another domain, yours or someone else's, holds the name, or when the name no longer passes the hostname check.
GET /api/v1/admin/domains leaves removed domains out unless status=DELETED is given, which lists only them, newest removal first, and can be sorted by deletedAt.
GET /api/v1/analytics/overview has a breakdowns object, in the same shape as a link's analytics.
The webhook summaries have the new moreLinks, moreDeadLinks and moreEndingSoon fields.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: The MCP Registry listing shows the hrva.cc icon, and the server version is 2.28.0.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Status tags on admin All URLs show in full, and the status and owner columns appear only where the table has room beside the Actions column.
Every dropdown has space before its arrow.
The passkey sign-in method on Settings has a Manage passkeys button that takes you to your passkeys.
Proton Pass no longer offers a two-step code on Settings.
While hrva.cc restarts, pages keep trying for two minutes instead of showing an error, and the session check keeps loading.
Pages keep their own tab title when opened directly, and the sign-in, account and egg pages show the same title as in the page source.
Recent UTM tags are remembered on this device, the last five for each field, with a Clear button under the fields to forget them. The privacy page says so.
A late reply to the session check can no longer sign you back in after you sign out.

releases.summary: Edit a link from the dashboard, turn expired and used-up links back on and change where a link points, ask for more custom domains, and see where an app will send you before you allow it.

sections.title: Links
items: Each link in the dashboard has an Edit action. Change or remove its visit limit and expiry, add, change or remove its password, and change its tags.

An expired or used-up link opens in the same form. Set a later expiry or a higher visit limit, and the same save can turn it back on. Turning a link back on checks its destination again, like a new link.

You can change where a link points. A link on hrva.cc needs an account in good standing: two-step sign-in on, the account at least 30 days old, a verified email or sign-in with Google or GitHub, and none of your links blocked, being checked, or blocked in the last 90 days. A link on your own custom domain can change without these. A link made without an account can't change.
When a destination can't change yet, the Edit form lists what is missing, such as "Turn on two-step sign-in" or the date it becomes available.

An admin can set an account to Always allowed or Never allowed for destination changes, from the account's admin page. Never allowed also covers links on your own domain, and the Edit form then says that an admin turned off destination changes for your account.
A link's destination can change 5 times a day.
Activating a link that used all its clicks or has expired says to edit it first, and the help pages and the bio page hint point to Edit.

sections.title: Custom Domains
items: An account at its custom domain limit can ask for more from the Custom domains card in Settings: say how many in total, up to 20, and what for. An admin approves or declines it, and you get an email either way. One request can wait at a time, and you can withdraw it while it waits.

sections.title: Link Safety
items: A new destination gets the same checks as a new link. A destination that would be refused for a new link is refused, and one that would be sent to review is saved and sent to review.
Admins can turn destination changes off for everyone in Site settings.

Admins can edit every field of any link. When an admin's new destination would be blocked or sent to review, the admin is shown why and has to save it again to confirm, and the change is marked as confirmed in the link's history.
A link made without an account no longer passes the visitor's query string on: it opens its destination exactly as it was checked.
When a value passed on in a short link's query is a web address hrva.cc would block, the query isn't passed on, and the link opens its destination as saved.

sections.title: Security
items: The screen where you allow an AI app to use your account now shows where the app will send you, and warns when an app uses the name of a well-known app but sends you somewhere else.
You now get an email when an app is connected to your account for the first time, with a link to disconnect it.
A Google or GitHub sign-in can now only be finished in the browser that started it.

While hrva.cc's request counters are unavailable, it now pauses what could be abused instead of letting it through: API key requests, making links, account emails, link previews, bio page changes, custom domain applications and retries, requests for more custom domains and destination changes answer "try again in a minute". Short links keep working.

sections.title: API
items: PUT /api/v1/urls/{id} works with an API key for your own links, under the same rules as the dashboard. It takes active to turn a link back on or off, and answers 429 with Retry-After on the sixth destination change of the day.

GET /api/v1/urls/{id}/destination-change says whether a link's destination can change and lists what is missing, and a refused change answers 403 with the same list. The developers page documents both.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: MCP tool descriptions say when to use each tool and what happens when a call is refused.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Every destination change is kept with its link: the old and new destination, when, and which account made it. Admins can read it, and the audit log records it too. The privacy and security pages say so.
Your account export now includes the destination history of your links, when one of your links was last blocked, and an admin's setting for your account's destination changes.
Requests for more custom domains are in your account export, and are deleted with your account.

sections.title: Admin
items: Admin Domains has a Limit requests page to approve or decline requests for more custom domains, paged, sorted and searchable, and the review count includes waiting requests.

releases.summary: The blog posts from May rewritten to match what hrva.cc does today, and a plain heading on the blog.

sections.title: Site
items: The twelve blog posts from May are rewritten so each one matches hrva.cc as it is now: the guides on why to use a URL shortener, link analytics, expiration dates and visit limits, and best practices, and the posts on database migrations, background work, caching, Google Safe Browsing, the audit log, the Angular rewrite, the interface and open source. Each shows the date it was updated, and eight have new titles that say what they cover.
The blog's heading is now simply Blog.

releases.summary: A security page that lists what hrva.cc checks and protects and how to report a vulnerability, security blog posts rewritten for today, and emails signed off with hrva.cc.

sections.title: Security
items: A new Security page at app.hrva.cc/security lists what hrva.cc checks before a short link sends someone on, how accounts, API keys and connected apps are protected, how the site itself is protected, and how to report a vulnerability. It is linked from the footer, the homepage and the help.
security.txt now points to the Security page.

sections.title: Site
items: "Why Safe Browsing Matters for Link Sharing" and "How hrva.cc Handles Security, Speed, Reliability, and Migration" are rewritten to match what hrva.cc does today, and "How hrva.cc stops phishing links" now covers the warning page and links held for a sign-in form. A rewritten post shows the date it was updated.
Emails end with "Best regards, hrva.cc".

sections.title: Privacy
items: The privacy page says exactly what is kept about signing in: the audit log records admin actions and changes to sign-in methods, not sign-ins. An account keeps when it last signed in and when each passkey or sign-in method was last used, and failed attempts are short-lived counters.

sections.title: Fixes
items: A tab left open across an update reloads itself once when it can't load part of the site, instead of showing an error such as "Couldn't load these stats".

releases.summary: Retry-After that gives the seconds left, the hrva.cc icon and a small not-found page for addresses on hrva.cc that aren't short links, an error status on the unavailable page, links to Revolut's and PayPal's privacy terms, and dependency and security updates.

sections.title: Links
items: An address on hrva.cc that isn't a short link, such as hrva.cc/robots.txt or hrva.cc/a/b, answers 404 with the small not-found page instead of an error in JSON. Short links and the API answer as before.
hrva.cc/favicon.ico is the hrva.cc icon, so the not-found and unavailable pages on hrva.cc show it in the browser tab.
The unavailable page a password-protected link can lead to answers with an error status, 404 or 410 like the short link itself, instead of 200. Its text stays the same.

sections.title: API
items: Retry-After on a 429 is the number of seconds until that limit resets, not the length of its whole window. This applies to every limit, from creating links to reports and connected app registration.

sections.title: Privacy
items: The privacy page explains the donation buttons: each one is a hrva.cc short link, so the click is counted like any other short-link visit, then your browser goes to Revolut or PayPal. hrva.cc sends them nothing beyond that redirect. It links to each company's own privacy terms.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Updated dependencies, and fixed a pattern that a very long link could make slow.

releases.summary: Visit limits that count every click and can't be passed at once, query strings passed on to the destination, 201 Created with the full short link, an API closed unless a route is public, final API key revokes, admin pages that need two-step sign-in, password reset links that work once for an hour, sign-up that never shows whether an email is taken, API keys as Bearer tokens, stricter checks of the pages hrva.cc fetches, and quick 503 answers when Redis or the database can't answer.

sections.title: Accounts & Security
items: You get an email 30 days before an account is deactivated for 5 years without use. Signing in, using an API key or using a connected MCP app keeps it active.
If the sign-in counters can't be reached, signing in with a password pauses for a minute instead of going unlimited. The message says when to try again.
A password reset link works once and for 1 hour, and only a hash of it is stored. Links sent before this release no longer work; ask for a new one.
Setting a new password from a reset link no longer asks for your email. The link already names the account.
Asking for a password reset or a new verification email is limited per network and per email address, so nobody can flood an inbox. The answer never says whether an account uses the address.
Signing up with an email that already has an account answers the same as a new sign-up. The account gets an email saying someone tried, with links to sign in and reset the password.
Revoking an API key is final. A revoked or expired key can't be turned back on, only deleted; make a new key instead. The Activate buttons are gone.

sections.title: Link Safety
items: When hrva.cc fetches a destination to follow its redirects, see whether it still works or read its preview, it connects only to the address it checked, and checks again on every redirect.

For some links made without an account that open the warning page, hrva.cc reads the destination page once after the link is made. A page with a sign-in or card form puts the link on hold until an admin checks it. Until then, visitors are told the link is being checked.
Links to a well-known brand's name on a domain ending the brand doesn't use, such as amazon.xyz, are flagged for review.

sections.title: Links
items: A visit limit now counts every click, not counting bots, so a link limited to 5 opens 5 times, even for the same visitor. The count is checked before the redirect, so clicks at the same moment can't go past the limit. Links with a limit keep the visits they had used. Unique visitors in your stats count as before.

A short link passes its query string on: hrva.cc/abc?ref=mail opens the destination with ref=mail added. The destination's own parameters win when both have the same name, hrva.cc's qr marker isn't passed on, and the destination's #fragment stays.
New random aliases leave out 0, O, 1, l and I, so they're easier to read out and type. Aliases stay case-sensitive, and existing ones don't change.

Link previews are kept for 10 minutes. A network can ask for 30 previews a minute, and a link's page is fetched at most 10 times in 10 minutes. Over the limit, or while 8 previews are already being fetched, the answer says when to try again.

While the rate limiter is down, links without an account aren't made and the link-password check waits: both answer 503 with Retry-After instead of letting requests through. Signed-in, API-key and AI connector links are made as usual.
When the database doesn't answer, a short link that isn't cached answers 503 within a few seconds instead of waiting, and cached links keep working.

sections.title: API
items: Creating a link answers 201 Created with a Location header and the full short link in shortLink, with or without an API key or an account. Bulk creates answer 200 as before, each link with its shortLink.

The API answers without a sign-in only on a listed set of public routes, such as short links, link lookups, creating a link and signing in. Anything else, including a wrong method or an unknown path, is a 401 until you sign in.
POST /api/v1/auth/register answers 202 with a JSON body, the same for a new and a taken address. POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm answers 204 with no body.
An API key also works as Authorization: Bearer <key>, besides X-Api-Key. A Bearer value that starts with hrva_ is read as a key, anything else as a sign-in.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Email addresses are masked in every server log line.
Counters for password reset and verification emails keep a hash of the network or email address for an hour, never the address itself.

sections.title: Admin
items: Admin pages and the MCP moderation tools need two-step sign-in on the admin's account. Until it's on, they answer "Turn on two-step sign-in to use admin pages." and the dashboard opens the two-step settings. Your own account pages keep working.
The Health page lists each blocklist with its last refresh, its errors in a row and whether it is stale. A list that misses two refreshes sends the owner one email.
A held link that gets its final block closes its review with the reason of that block, the same as any other block: a domain block as "domain blocked", its own blocklist hit as "link blocked".
A link without an account whose same-shape hold was lifted while it was being made still gets the warning page and the random-domain review when its domain calls for them.

releases.summary: Sign out everywhere, a one-time code instead of any token in the address bar, sign-in limits per account and per network, standard API errors and UTC dates, real statuses for dead links, and a content security policy for the dashboard.

sections.title: Accounts & Security
items: Sign out everywhere in Settings signs out every other browser and device. The one you use stays signed in. API keys and connected apps keep working.
Changing your password, removing it, or turning off Google or GitHub sign-in signs out your other devices. Resetting a forgotten password signs out every device.
Signing in with Google or GitHub no longer puts a token of any kind in the address bar, with two-step verification on too. The sign-in page swaps a one-time code for it.
Passwords can be up to 72 bytes; accented letters count as two. A longer one shows a message under the field instead of an error.

After too many wrong passwords for one account, or from one network, sign-in pauses for up to 15 minutes or an hour. The message says how long to wait. Signing into a different account in between resets neither count.
A role taken away from an account stops working on its next request, not when its sign-in expires.
The dashboard sends a content security policy, so pages load scripts only from hrva.cc and Cloudflare Turnstile and can't be framed by other sites.

sections.title: Links
items: A link that doesn't exist answers 404, and one that is blocked, expired, used up or turned off answers 410, with a short page that says why. Before, they redirected to a page that answered 200.
A HEAD request to a short link answers like a visit but counts no click and uses no visit, so link checkers and uptime monitors don't use up a visit limit.
A short link with a slash at the end, like hrva.cc/abc/, opens the same link.

sections.title: API
items: API errors use the standard problem details format (RFC 9457).
Every date and time in the API is in UTC with a Z, like 2026-10-30T19:02:13Z. Dates you send without an offset are still read as UTC.
A request that needs a signed-in account answers 401 when nobody is signed in, and 403 only when the account isn't allowed. Every 429 says how long to wait in a Retry-After header.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Sign-in attempt counters keep a hash of the network or email address, never the address itself.

sections.title: Admin
items: Login rate limits in Stats › System show counters per network and per account. They survive restarts, and you can search them by IP address or email.

sections.title: Site
items: The developers page covers dates, error answers, status codes and what a short link answers.

releases.summary: An hourly rate limit for API keys instead of a lifetime cap, a key expiry you choose, and keys stored hashed.

sections.title: API Keys
items: API keys no longer stop working after a fixed number of calls. Each key can make 600 requests an hour, and a key over the limit is told when to try again.
You choose when a new API key expires, or that it never does.
API keys are stored hashed: the full key is shown once when you make it.

sections.title: Admin
items: Site settings sets how many requests an API key can make in an hour.

releases.summary: A human check and a warning page for links made without an account, limits on those links, and sign-in switches.

sections.title: Link Safety
items: Some links made without an account open a short warning page first. It shows the full destination, with Continue and Report this link.
Making a link without an account runs a quick Cloudflare Turnstile check on the homepage, /qr, /utm and /share. Signed-in users, API keys and MCP are never checked.
Links made without an account can have an end date or a visit limit set by hrva.cc. The form says so when they do.

sections.title: Privacy
items: The Turnstile check processes browser and network signals for that check only. hrva.cc stores nothing from it.

sections.title: Site
items: The help page for links made without an account now covers limits, the human check and the warning page.

sections.title: Admin
items: Links made without an account to random-looking new domains go to the review queue.
The warning page can be cleared on a link in All URLs.
Sign in with Google and Sign in with GitHub can each be turned off in Settings.

releases.summary: Campaign holds and abuse reports.

sections.title: Admin
items: Links made without an account that share one URL shape across several domains are now held, with one Discord alert per campaign.
A new Campaigns page lists each held URL shape with its links, domains, clicks and report status, with Block all domains, Report all and Allow this shape.
Report domains prepares one abuse email per registrar for the ticked links' domains, to open in your mail app or copy. Reported domains are checked daily and marked when they are suspended.
Settings has new values for campaign holds (on or off, and how many days a hold lasts) and for abuse reports (your name and address, the Cc and how many days reported domains are rechecked).

releases.summary: An admin Settings page: turn features on or off and change their numbers without a redeploy, emails included.

sections.title: Links
items: When making links without an account is paused, the homepage, /qr and /utm say so before you type. When new sign-ups are paused, the register page says so.

sections.title: Security
items: You can turn off Google or GitHub sign-in, or remove your password, in Settings. The last way you sign in can't be removed.

sections.title: Admin
items: A new Settings page: turn features on or off and change their numbers without a redeploy. Every change is logged and posted to Discord, and a safety check that is off shows a warning on Settings and Stats.
Emails can be turned off all at once or one kind at a time. Account emails always go out, and an email a switch stopped shows as Not sent in the email log.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains links made without an account and when making them is paused.

releases.summary: Discord alerts when links made without an account share one URL shape or get busy, every way you've signed in listed in Settings, and admin lists searched, sorted and paged on the server.

sections.title: Links
items: Searching your links waits until you stop typing, and stays in the address.
Your API keys are listed newest first, and expired or revoked keys a page at a time.

sections.title: Security
items: Settings lists every way you've signed in, with when you last used it.

sections.title: Admin
items: Discord alerts when links made without an account share one URL shape across several domains.

Discord alerts when a link made without an account gets many clicks in a day, or when such links take most of the day's clicks. The daily email lists yesterday's busiest links made without an account.
Blocking many domains at once saves every block rule first, and asks you to try again if it stops halfway.
Every admin list can be searched and sorted, page by page.
Domain rules are listed page by page, with a search box and a choice of order.
Custom domains can be sorted by name, status or date added.
Users shows every sign-in method an account has used.

releases.summary: Custom domains: apply for your own subdomain, like go.example.com, and make short links on it.

sections.title: Links
items: Apply for a custom domain in Settings, under Custom domains. Once it's approved, add one CNAME record and hrva.cc sets up the certificate for you.
Pick your domain when you shorten a link. Aliases on your domain are your own: go.example.com/menu and hrva.cc/menu can both exist.
Short links on your domain work like any other: stats, visit limits, passwords and expiry dates.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Visitors to your domain get the same privacy as visitors to hrva.cc. Cloudflare receives your domain's name to issue its certificate.

sections.title: Admin
items: A new Domains page: review applications, see every domain with its owner, links and clicks, turn domains off, retry, or remove them with their links moved or turned off.
Cloudflare custom hostnames are created and deleted automatically after approval, never beyond the cap of 90, and checked against Cloudflare every night.
Pending applications count in the review badge, and the stats page shows domains against the cap.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains custom domains, with the exact DNS record for common providers.

releases.summary: Sign in with GitHub, verified email addresses for Google and GitHub sign-ins, and hrva.cc as an installable app.

sections.title: Security
items: Sign in with GitHub. hrva.cc uses your GitHub account's verified primary email.
Signing in with Google now needs a verified email address.
When new sign-ups are paused, Google and GitHub can't create accounts either.
Signing in with Google or GitHub to an account whose email address was never confirmed confirms it and turns off the password it was created with.
If signing in with Google or GitHub fails, you come back to hrva.cc with a message instead of a bare error page.

sections.title: Site
items: hrva.cc can be installed as an app. On Android you can share a link to it from any app to shorten it.
A Support section on the About page.

releases.summary: Admins can block the domains of several links at once.

sections.title: Admin
items: Block domains on All URLs blocks the domains of the ticked links at once, after showing how many active links on the site each one turns off.

releases.summary: Notification settings that are easier to find and fix, and faster bio pages.

sections.title: Notifications
items: Adding or editing a channel shows every problem at once instead of one at a time.
Notifications now sits right below your profile and password in Settings, and a link marked "Destination looks dead" offers "Get an email when this happens" while dead-link emails are off.

sections.title: Links
items: Bio pages and their share images load faster: they're kept for up to 5 minutes, so saved changes can take up to 5 minutes to show, and your old handle can keep working for up to 5 minutes after you change it or delete your page. View page in the editor always shows the saved version.

releases.summary: Emails that match the site, and new pages: about, developers, a free QR code generator and UTM builder.

sections.title: Site
items: Emails have a new look that matches the site, easier to read on phones and in dark mode.
New About page: who runs hrva.cc, how it is paid for and how to reach it.
New page on how hrva.cc counts visits without tracking, with what it keeps, what it never stores and the source code to check.
New developers page with an API quickstart in curl, JavaScript and Python, the request fields, errors and limits. The MCP page now has example prompts and says what your assistant can see.
Free QR code generator at /qr: no account, PNG and SVG download, and an optional short link to count scans.
Free UTM builder at /utm: tag any link without an account, copy it or shorten it.
New link in bio page explaining bio pages, linked from the header and from the bottom of every bio page.
The homepage API example now shows the real response code, 200 OK.

releases.summary: Clearer notification channel messages: a deleted Discord or Slack webhook says so, saved secrets keep a visible note, and a channel with no events ticked says it gets nothing.

sections.title: Notifications
items: If Discord or Slack no longer knows a channel's webhook, Send test and the channel say it may have been deleted and ask you to copy the webhook URL again.
When you edit a channel, the note that a saved address or token is kept if you leave the field empty stays visible while you type.
The channel dialog says when no event is ticked, so the channel won't get any messages yet.
Pasting an ntfy topic URL into a webhook channel now calls it an ntfy topic URL.

releases.summary: Notifications you choose: dead-link checks, a weekly summary, and alerts to Discord, Slack, Telegram, ntfy, a webhook or email.

sections.title: Links
items: hrva.cc now checks every active link's destination each night. If it fails three different nights, with no working answer in between (the page is gone, or the website no longer exists), the link is marked "Destination looks dead" on your dashboard and in its stats.

sections.title: Notifications
items: New Notifications settings: get an email when a link stops working, a weekly summary every Monday, or a reminder before a link expires. Everything is off until you turn it on.

Add channels for Discord, Slack, Telegram, ntfy or your own webhook (signed JSON), and pick which events each gets: a link stopped working, a link works again, a daily click summary or the weekly summary. Each channel has Send test and shows its last delivery.
Expiry reminders are now opt-in. If you want them, turn on Expiry reminders in Settings, under Notifications.
Every notification email has a one-click unsubscribe link.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Notifications carry counts, short links and destination hosts only, never visitors' IP addresses, browsers or referrers. Channel URLs and tokens are encrypted. After you save them, URLs and bot tokens are shown masked, and other tokens are never shown again.
We no longer send a welcome email after you verify your address.

sections.title: Admin
items: All URLs can show only links whose destination looks dead, and the stats page counts them, plus notification opt-ins and channels per type.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains notifications, channels and webhook signatures step by step.

releases.summary: Admins can delete expired and revoked API keys, logs are no longer kept forever, pages load faster, and three API key fixes.

sections.title: API Keys
items: Admins can delete expired and revoked API keys from All API keys.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Email logs are deleted after 90 days and the admin audit log after 12 months.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Deleting an API key that was already removed says so instead of asking you to revoke it.
Keyboard focus stays in the API keys table after you revoke a key.
Creating a link with an API key no longer undoes a revoke made at the same moment, and links created at once with one key all count.
Pages load faster and no longer fail when many people visit at once.

releases.summary: A tidier header and footer, expired and revoked API keys you can delete, and short links guaranteed unique.

sections.title: Site
items: The header now has Bio pages, Developers, Help and Check a link; Blog and Changelog moved to the footer, and the stats page is listed as Public stats.

sections.title: API Keys
items: Expired and revoked API keys can be deleted, one at a time or all at once, and they're tucked away below your active keys.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Short links are now guaranteed unique in the database.
On the report page, sending keeps keyboard focus on the Send button even after a double click.

releases.summary: Bio pages: one page with all your links, for your Instagram, TikTok or any other bio.

sections.title: Links
items: Bio pages: make a page at hrva.cc/@yourname with your name, a short bio, an emoji or initials avatar and a button for each of your short links. Pick a colour and a light, dark or automatic theme, reorder buttons by dragging or with the keyboard, hide one without deleting it, and see a live preview as you edit.
Your bio keeps its line breaks, up to five lines, so each detail can go on its own line.

If your bio page changed in another tab or window, saving an older copy doesn't overwrite it: the editor loads the latest version, keeps your unsaved changes and asks you to check them and save again.

Every button is one of your own short links, so each click gets the same safety checks as any other link. A link that stops working, is blocked or is waiting for review disappears from your page, and the editor shows why.
Share your page with a copy-link button or a QR code from the Bio page screen.
When you share your page in a chat or on social media, its preview image shows your name, your @handle and your initials in your colour.

sections.title: Analytics
items: A Bio page view on the Analytics page shows views per day and, for each button, clicks that came from hrva.cc pages and all clicks on its link.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Bio page views are counted once per visitor per day with the same daily-changing one-way hash as link statistics. No IP address or browser details are stored, and the page loads no third-party scripts, fonts or trackers.
Search engines are asked not to list your page unless you turn on "Allow search engines to index this page".

sections.title: Link Safety
items: Anyone can report a bio page with "Report this page" at the bottom of it, or on the Report a link page with hrva.cc/@name.
Reports have a new category, "Pretends to be someone", for a link or bio page that impersonates a person or a business.

sections.title: Admin
items: Bio pages: search pages by handle, name or owner, hide a page with a reason, and change or revoke a handle. A revoked handle is added to the reserved aliases.

Reports, and text that looks like impersonation or phishing, put a bio page in the review queue with Looks fine and Hide page. Discord hears about new bio page reviews and reports, and the daily decisions email counts them.
The stats page shows how many bio pages there are and how many views they had.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains bio pages step by step, linked from the Bio page screen and the Help center.

releases.summary: QR scans in link analytics, a public page with hrva.cc in numbers, a weekly summary and phishing-wave alerts for the admin, and the AI connector is sign-in only.

sections.title: Analytics
items: QR codes made by hrva.cc now count their scans: link analytics and the admin stats split clicks into QR scans and other clicks. Codes made before this release count as other clicks, so download a new code to count scans from it.

sections.title: Site
items: hrva.cc in numbers: a public page with site-wide totals for the last 30 days, such as active links, clicks per day, harmful links blocked and how fast reports are reviewed. It never shows anything about a single link or person.
A new help page explains the public numbers and QR scans, linked from both and from the Help page.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: The AI connector without an account (hrva.cc/mcp/anon) is gone. Connect hrva.cc/mcp and sign in instead.

sections.title: Admin
items: Weekly summary: every Monday morning, Discord and email get last week's clicks, visitors, bot share, new links and users, reviews and automatic blocks, the top 5 links, and how many reviews are waiting right now. Clicks, new links and new users are compared with the week before. Discord and email can be turned off separately.

Phishing-wave alert: Discord warns when 5 or more new links to the same new or unknown domain appear within an hour from at least 2 different accounts or networks, with a link to those links. Nothing is blocked automatically.
All URLs opens with a search from its address, so the alert's link lands on the matching links.

sections.title: Privacy
items: The public numbers page stores nothing about you beyond a rate-limit counter for your network, which expires after an hour. QR scans are a daily count per link, like the other link statistics.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Discord alerts for the admin show links, domains, reasons and visitor details in full instead of cutting them off with "…". Alerts that don't fit in one message are counted as "and N more".
Searching links, users or the review queue for % or _ now finds those characters instead of matching everything.
Searching links for a domain finds it in either spelling, such as čokolada.hr and xn--okolada-i6a.hr.
A web address whose domain name is longer than 253 characters, the most a domain name can have, is now refused as not a valid web address.
Signing in again from an admin page brings you back to the page you opened.
The report and unavailable pages no longer show the footer twice.
Password managers no longer offer to fill your username into a passkey's name.

releases.summary: Passkeys and security keys, and two-step verification for every sign-in method.

sections.title: Security
items: Sign in with a passkey: your fingerprint, face or screen lock, a password manager such as Bitwarden, Proton Pass or 1Password, or a security key such as a YubiKey. No password to type.
Add as many passkeys and security keys as you like in Settings, and rename or remove them there. You get an email whenever one is added.
Two-step verification can use a passkey or security key instead of a code, and can be turned on with passkeys only.
Google and GitHub sign-ins now ask for your second step when two-step verification is on, and accounts that use Google or GitHub can turn it on.
Recovery and authenticator codes work however you type them, with or without spaces, dashes or capitals.
Sign-in messages now say how many tries are left and when you can try again.
Deleting an account that signs in with Google or GitHub needs a sign-in within the last 15 minutes, as adding or removing a passkey does.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Passkeys store only a public key and a few details, such as the name you give it, when it was added and last used, and whether it's synced. Your fingerprint, face and PIN never leave your device.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains passkeys and security keys step by step, linked from Settings and the footer.

releases.summary: Campaign tracking tags for your links, a full statistics page and reserved short link names for the admin, and a simpler admin menu.

sections.title: Links
items: Campaign tracking (UTM): when you create or edit a link, add Source, Medium and Campaign tags in a few clicks, with a preview of the final link. Your analytics tool reads them; hrva.cc doesn't.

sections.title: Analytics
items: Link analytics shows the full destination's campaign tags (UTM) when the link has them.

sections.title: Admin
items: Stats: one page with Traffic, Links, Users, Safety and System tabs for the last 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. It shows clicks and visitors across all links, top links and referrers, links created per day and how they were made, sign-ups, the review queue and blocks, and the server's health.
Long values are shown in full and wrap, instead of being cut off with "…".
The stats are totals only. Unique visitors are counted per link per day and added up, and nothing identifies a visitor.
Reserved aliases: keep short link names back, each with a reason. Nobody can create a link with one, random links never pick one, and links that already use one keep working.
New links remember how they were made: on the website, with an API key, in bulk or through the AI connector, with or without an account.
The admin pages have their own sidebar, grouped into Overview, Moderation, Content and Logs, in place of one long menu.
The dashboard's redirect timing, request count, cache hit ratio, app version and database and Redis status now show real values.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Admin pages show times in your own time zone.
Removing a reserved alias or a domain rule keeps keyboard focus on the list.
Look-alike links that mix alphabets, such as a Cyrillic letter in a well-known brand, are now caught and sent for review.
If an admin blocks a whole domain or several links at once, each owner now gets one email listing their blocked links instead of one email per link.
Sign-up refuses an email address that's too long before sending any email.

releases.summary: Fixes for reactivating links, addresses with accented letters, admin link edits and blocklist refreshes.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Reactivating a link works again, including when an admin unblocks a blocked link.
Links to addresses with accented letters, such as čokolada.hr, now redirect.
Older links whose address contains curly braces now redirect instead of showing an error.
When an admin changes a link's destination, the old destination's redirect details no longer come back, and a block made at the same moment is kept.
A refused link edit, such as an expiry date in the past, is no longer saved anyway.
Refreshing a blocklist source no longer undoes a change another admin made during the download, such as turning it off.

releases.summary: Fixes for long links and for two people picking the same short link name.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Links whose destination is longer than 255 characters no longer fail. Destinations can be up to 2048 characters, and longer ones get a clear message.
If two people pick the same custom short link name at the same moment, the second now gets "This short URL is already taken. Try another." instead of an error.
Bulk creation now answers an invalid link with a clear message instead of a server error.

releases.summary: Small fixes: header links when signed in, an accurate AI connector page and an up-to-date changelog.

sections.title: Fixes
items: The Features and API links in the header now work when you're signed in: the home page shows those sections below your shorten form.
The AI connector page no longer lists the no-account server, which can't create links while anonymous link creation is turned off.
This changelog covers everything since May again.

sections.title: Site
items: Blog posts and the privacy and terms pages link to the author's site, karlo.cc.

releases.summary: Privacy-first link analytics with referrers, countries and devices, plus Discord alerts and bulk review for the admin.

sections.title: Analytics
items: Rebuilt analytics for each link: clicks per day, daily unique visitors and bot clicks, with its top referrers, countries, devices, browsers and operating systems.
Rebuilt analytics overview across all your links, with a daily trend and your top 10 links by clicks.
Pick a range of 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. Times are shown in your own time zone.
Bots, link previews and crawlers, including the check Outlook runs before it opens a link, are counted separately and never as clicks or visits.
Bots and link previews can no longer use up a visit-limited link: they aren't sent to its destination.
A link's visit count now counts each person once per day and leaves bots out.
Daily statistics start on 24 October 2026. Earlier clicks are included only in a link's all-time visit count.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Link statistics are daily totals per link. Nothing is recorded about an individual click, and IP addresses are never stored for link statistics.

To count unique visitors, the IP address and browser identifier are combined with the link and a random key that changes every day into a one-way hash. The hashes and the key are kept only in Redis, never in the database, and expire a few hours after the day ends, so a visitor can't be followed across days or links.
The country comes from Cloudflare, which carries hrva.cc's traffic; hrva.cc doesn't look up locations itself.
The old visit records, which held a hashed IP address for each visitor, have been deleted.
The privacy policy and the home page describe the new daily statistics.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: link_stats now takes a range of 7, 30, 90 or 365 days and shows a link's top referrers, countries and devices, next to its clicks, daily unique visitors and bot clicks.

sections.title: Admin
items: Discord alerts: hrva.cc posts to the admin's Discord channel when a link is flagged for review or reported by a visitor, when a link is blocked automatically, when someone signs up, and when a blocklist fails to load or loads again. Alerts are sent together every 30 seconds and never include email or IP addresses.
Review queue: select up to 100 entries and resolve them in one go. A domain they share is blocked or trusted once for all of them.
Audit log: every entry has a readable action name, failed actions are marked, and the log can be filtered by action.

releases.summary: Layered checks against phishing and malware, a page for reporting links, and a review queue for doubtful ones.

sections.title: Link Safety
sections.description: hrva.cc now checks where links lead when they're created, every night, and on every click.
items: New links are checked against public blocklists of harmful domains and exact links (HaGeZi, OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus and Phishing.Database). hrva.cc downloads the lists to its own server and refreshes them regularly, so checking a link against them sends it nowhere.
hrva.cc also checks how old a destination's domain is, looks it up in the Spamhaus domain blocklist, and watches for names that imitate well-known brands or pose as login pages.
A destination known to be harmful can't be shortened. A doubtful one is saved and sent to a person for review instead of being blocked.
After a link is created, hrva.cc follows its redirects in the background and checks every address along the way.
Every night, all active links are checked again against Google Safe Browsing and the latest lists.
Every click is checked against the blocking lists first. A link whose destination has been listed since it was created stops working on that click.
If one of your links is blocked, you get an email. If a whole account is blocked, its owner gets a single email.

sections.title: Reports & Unavailable Links
items: Anyone can report a hrva.cc link for phishing, malware, spam or other abuse on the new Report a link page. Reports go to a person for review and never block a link on their own.

A short link that doesn't work now opens a page saying why: it was disabled for leading to a harmful site, it expired, it reached its visit limit, its owner turned it off, or it doesn't exist. The page has a button to report the link.
hrva.cc publishes its abuse contact, abuse@hrva.cc, at hrva.cc/.well-known/security.txt.

sections.title: Blog & Policies
items: New blog post: How hrva.cc stops phishing links. It covers the scam links found in September, what hrva.cc checks now, and what it still can't catch.
The privacy policy and terms of use have new sections on how links are checked, reported and moderated, and on which services see a destination's domain or URL.

sections.title: Admin
items: Blocklists page: add, edit and refresh list sources, each with fallback mirrors and its own refresh interval; see each list's size and last error; manage Block and Allow rules for domains; and test any URL to see every check that matches it.
Review queue for flagged and reported links, with Looks fine, Trust domain, Block link, Block domain and Block user. The admin menu shows how many entries are waiting.

Blocking a domain switches off every active link to it and its subdomains at once. Trusting a domain clears its reviews and, after checking them again, restores its links that a blocklist, scam signals or a domain rule had blocked.
Blocking a user deactivates the account and blocks its links; unblocking restores both, after a confirmation that names the user.
All URLs shows why a link was blocked, and domains and users can be blocked straight from the table.
Accounts that behave like typical scam accounts are marked as possible scammers, with a filter on the Users page. The marker never blocks anything by itself.

The daily admin email became a decisions email: it's sent only when something needs a decision and lists open reviews, automatic blocks, possible scammers and failing lists, without the text visitors wrote.

Admins can moderate from Claude or ChatGPT through the AI connector: read the review queue and possible scammers, check a URL, block links, domains and users, and delete links. These tools can't unblock or trust anything and won't change more than 50 links at once. Deleting a link, blocking a domain or blocking a user needs a flag or block from the automatic checks first, since a visitor report alone isn't enough. Users appear only as masked email addresses.

releases.summary: Fixes from a security scan, working email sign-up, an hourly limit on new links, and admin tools for spotting abuse.

sections.title: Security
items: Account details returned by the API, including the response to a password reset, no longer include the password hash.
Previews, QR codes and other public lookups of a short link no longer show the owner's email or tags, and keep a password-protected link's destination hidden until it's unlocked.
Wrong passwords on protected links are rate limited, and wrong two-factor codes count against the account.
Setting up two-factor authentication again no longer switches off the one that's already active.
A custom alias stays taken after its link expires or is turned off, so nobody else can claim it.
Link previews never fetch private or internal network addresses, on any redirect.
New passwords need at least 8 characters.
Link passwords are no longer written to the admin audit log, and older entries were cleaned up.

sections.title: Links
items: Each account can create up to 60 links an hour, across the website, API keys and AI apps. Every link in a bulk upload counts.
Links to other URL shorteners, or back to hrva.cc, are refused. Share links such as t.co, lnkd.in and Google's share links still work.
You can reactivate links you turned off yourself.
The nightly Safe Browsing check no longer skips links, and a link it blocks can't be reactivated by its owner.
Reactivating a link checks it with Safe Browsing again and makes sure no other link holds its alias.
Short links keep working when the cache is down, and a link stops as soon as it reaches its visit limit.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Signing up with email and password works again. The form now confirms the sign-up and shows what to fix in each field instead of "Request failed".
Reminder emails for links that are about to expire are sent again.
Signing in or out clears data left over from the previous session, and a network error no longer signs you out.
Deleting the last link on the last page goes back a page, and selecting links for a bulk action only picks the ones on the page you see.
Check a link says when a link is password protected instead of showing an empty destination.
Settings shows your sign-in email as read-only, instead of an email form that couldn't save.

sections.title: Admin
items: Resend failed emails from the email log. Emails stuck sending for 10 minutes are marked failed, and stored email content is deleted once it's sent, or after 7 days if sending failed.
All URLs: search by owner email or a pasted hrva.cc/abc link, show anonymous links only, sort by owner, and see a Suspicious marker with its reasons. The delete button works again.

Suspicious-link flags for lookalike brand names, login lures, high-risk domain endings, dynamic DNS hosts, raw IP addresses, punycode and chained shorteners. They only flag; nothing is switched off automatically.
A daily email lists new links from accounts younger than a week and links flagged as suspicious.
Audit log entries list only the fields that were sent, show a password as changed or removed, and label failed actions clearly.
Editing an API key's limits works again, and the health page reports email delivery from the latest email.

releases.summary: Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps to your hrva.cc account.

sections.title: AI Connector (MCP)
sections.description: hrva.cc now has an MCP server at hrva.cc/mcp.
items: Connect Claude (web, desktop and phone), Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or another MCP app that supports remote servers with sign-in, and it can shorten links into your account, list them and check their visits.
The app signs in through hrva.cc: you log in as usual, with your password and two-factor code or with Google, then allow or deny the app on a consent page.
Links an AI app creates are tagged "ai".
Settings → Connected apps lists each connected app with when it was first connected and last used. Disconnecting an app cuts off its access at once.
New MCP server page with setup steps for each app.
The privacy policy explains what is stored for connected apps and for how long.

sections.title: Links & Sign-in
items: A destination must be a real web address: http or https with a proper domain name. Anything else gets a clear error instead of becoming a broken link. A bare domain such as example.com still gets https:// added.
Signing in takes you back to the page you were trying to open.

sections.title: Security
items: Fixed a gap that let a signed-in user edit a link they didn't own. Only a link's owner or an admin can edit it now.

sections.title: Admin
items: Admins can change where a short link points. The new destination is checked with Google Safe Browsing first.

releases.summary: A new look, a new logo, and privacy and terms pages.

sections.title: Redesign
items: A fresh, modern design across the site, with a new logo and a cleaner light theme. Dark mode is still there and follows your system setting.
Every public page now shares the same header and footer.
The dashboard, admin pages, blog and changelog were restyled to match.

sections.title: Privacy & Terms
items: New Privacy Policy and Terms of Use pages, linked from the footer.
hrva.cc is a non-commercial hobby project of HrvaLabs, and the footer, privacy policy and terms link to the HrvaLabs website.

sections.title: Fixes
items: The home page fits on narrow phones, and the footer links wrap onto a new line instead of running off the screen.

releases.summary: Email verification, two-factor auth, account self-service, analytics, and URL tags.

sections.title: Accounts & Security
items: Email verification on registration — new accounts must confirm their email before signing in (existing users grandfathered, Google accounts auto-verified).
Two-factor authentication (TOTP) for password accounts, with one-time recovery codes and a second login step.
Account active status now enforced everywhere: deactivated users are blocked at login and per-request.
Self-service account deletion (password-confirmed) that removes the user and all their URLs and API keys.
Deactivating a user now revokes their API keys; an API key works only while both the key and its owner are active.

sections.title: URLs & Analytics
items: Password-protected links — lock a short URL behind a password (registered users); visitors enter it before the redirect resolves.
URL tags — organize links with tags, filter by tag, see them on the dashboard.
Per-URL and overview click analytics (visits, unique recent visitors, new-visitor trend).
URL and API-key status now shows the real reason: Active, Expired, Limit reached, Revoked, Deactivated, or Blocked.
Customizable QR codes — pick colors, size, and error-correction level, with PNG and SVG download.

sections.title: Admin & Privacy
items: Download-my-data export (profile, URLs, API keys, emails) as JSON.
Admin gets notified by email when a new user registers; dashboard shows new-user counts (7d / 30d).
Admin-only endpoints are hidden from the public API docs.

releases.summary: URL creation reliability, clearer errors, hardened validation.

sections.title: URL Creation Fixes
sections.description: Bare domains and pasted whitespace no longer break URL creation.
items: Auto-prepend https:// when the scheme is missing (e.g. test.gmail.com → https://test.gmail.com).
Trim leading/trailing whitespace on submitted URLs.
Persist-time validation failures now return 400 with a field-level error instead of 500.
Friendlier, end-user-oriented validation messages across the API.

sections.title: Routing & Safety Hardening
items: Reserved-word check for custom short URLs now matches exactly (case-insensitive) instead of prefix-match, so loginpage and apifoo are valid again.
Expanded reserved list: api, login, logout, oauth2, actuator, error, swagger-ui, v3, webjars, auth.
Bot probes (.env, favicon.ico, robots.txt, wp-login.php, etc.) return 404 silently — no log, no DB hit, no metric.
Custom short URL alias validated against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$ with 32-char cap.
Safe Browsing failures now log loudly with ALERT prefix; new app.safe-browsing-fail-closed flag to fail-closed when the API is unreachable.

sections.title: Auth & Config
items: Removed GitHub as an OAuth2 SSO provider. Google remains.
Short URL generation now uses RandomStringUtils.secureStrong() (SecureRandom) instead of the deprecated Math.random()-backed API.
OAuth2 user creation now persists once with active=true instead of INSERT + UPDATE.
app.google-api.key now bound to GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_KEY env var.

releases.summary: Search & filter your links, refined UX, better testing.

sections.title: URL & User Search / Filtering
sections.description: Find your links faster with powerful filters.
items: Dashboard: search input filters by long URL and short URL keywords.
Status dropdown (All / Active / Inactive) toggles visibility of deactivated links.
"Expired only" checkbox shows only links past their expiration date.
Date range pickers (dateFrom / dateTo) filter by creation date.
Admin users page: search by email and filter by active status.
Admin URLs page: search, status filter, expired-only checkbox, and sortable columns (Visits, Created).
Backend uses JPA Specifications for composable, dynamic queries.
Filter params bundled into UrlSearchDto / UserSearchDto instead of scattered @RequestParam annotations.

sections.title: Pagination Overhaul
items: Pagination bar is always visible — even on single-page results.
New "Showing X–Y of Z" total element count so you know the full scope.
Page size selector (10/20/50/100) with disabled prev/next buttons when at boundaries.
Applied to both dashboard (URLs) and admin (users) tables.

sections.title: Landing Page UX
items: Removed "Show advanced options" toggle from public hero form — custom alias, visit limit, and expiration silently didn't work for anonymous users. Now the form is dead-simple: paste URL → Shorten.
Logged-in form now shows alias, limit, and expiry directly without a toggle. Power users see the options immediately.
Hero subtitle updated to: "Shorten links in seconds. Sign up free for custom aliases, visit limits, expiration dates & analytics."
After shortening a link as anonymous user, a subtle upsell card appears: "Create a free account to set custom aliases, visit limits, and track analytics."
Status page link (status.hrva.cc) restored in footer — was lost in the React migration.
Footer now sticks to bottom of viewport using flex-1 layout.

sections.title: Sortable Columns
items: Dashboard: Visits, Created, and Expires columns are clickable with arrow indicators (↑↓↕).
Admin users: Email, Created, Last Login, and Status headers are sortable.
Admin URLs: Visits and Created columns are sortable.
Sort state persists in URL params (?sort=visits&order=asc) across page refreshes.
Default sort: URLs by newest first (createDate,desc), users by ID ascending.

sections.title: Admin URL Management
sections.description: Admins can now fully manage all URLs in the system.
items: Activate/deactivate toggle for any URL — deactivated URLs show a ToggleLeft icon to reactivate.
Edit dialog to change visit limit and expiration date on any URL.
New PATCH /api/v1/urls/{id}/activate endpoint on the backend.
Admin URLs page now has search, status filter, expired-only checkbox, and pagination with total count.
Row entrance animations and copy pulse on the admin URLs page.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Double scrollbar bug: removed overflow-x-hidden from root container — CSS spec was forcing overflow-y: auto, creating a nested scroll container.
Blur decorative elements now properly clipped with overflow-hidden on their section parents.
URL count on landing page stats bar now uses totalElements instead of content.length — showed wrong count when user had more than 20 URLs.
Deactivate toggle icon changed from ToggleLeft (ambiguous "off" position) to ToggleRight (clearly shows active URL can be turned off).

sections.title: Animations
items: Copy button pulse: brief scale bump (1→1.25→1) on copy for tactile feedback.
Staggered row entrance: table rows fade in one by one with 30-40ms delays.
Stats counter: landing page totals tick up from 0 with ease-out animation.
Filter cross-fade: table remounts on filter change, re-triggering entrance animation.

sections.title: Easter Eggs
items: Konami code (↑↑↓↓←→←→BA) — turns the page into a rainbow overlay for 5 seconds.
/fortune page — random URL-themed fortunes that refresh on each visit.
/egg page — a duck that quacks. Quack it 10 times for a surprise QR code.
Console message — opens dev tools to find a hint. ✨
Changelog footer — the see-no-evil monkey wiggles on hover.

sections.title: Admin Tools
sections.description: New admin capabilities for system management.
items: Audit Log table — every admin action (deactivate/activate/delete/update) is auto-logged with timestamp, admin email, and details via AOP aspect. Paginated view at /admin/audit-log.
Email Log table — all sent emails recorded with SENDING/SENT/FAILED status tracking. View delivery status at /admin/email-log.
System Health page — green/red status indicators for Database, Redis Cache, SMTP, and SafeBrowsing API.
Login Rate Limits viewer on admin dashboard — shows active IP rate limits with auto-refresh and clear-all button.
Bulk URL Management — checkbox selection on All URLs table with batch Activate/Deactivate/Delete actions.
New admin nav links: Health, Audit Log, Email Log.

sections.title: Cache Improvements
items: Redirect endpoint now cache-first: every GET /{short} checks Redis before DB, with validation on cache hit.
Cache warmup on startup: top 20 most visited, most recent, and recently accessed URLs pre-loaded into Redis.
Cache priming on creation: newly created URLs immediately cached.
TTL increased from 60 minutes to 7 days (stale data caught by validation on cache hit).
SafeBrowsing recheck scheduled task: daily at 2 AM, re-scans all active URLs against Google SafeBrowsing. Flagged URLs auto-deactivated and owner notified via email.

sections.title: Tests
items: 6 new unit tests for URL and User filtering (search, active, expired, date range).
2 new tests for URL activate endpoint and service method.
Updated existing tests to match new service and controller signatures.
3 new tests for scheduled safe browsing recheck and audit wiring.
Total: 150 tests, all passing (JUnit 5 + Mockito).

releases.summary: Complete frontend rewrite from Angular to React (Next.js). OAuth2 login, URL expiry notifications, performance overhaul.

sections.title: Frontend: Angular → React Rewrite
items: Complete rewrite from Angular to Next.js (React 19, App Router).
Server-side rendering for faster initial page loads and better SEO.
Dark/light theme toggle using next-themes with system preference detection.
Fully responsive layout optimized for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
Radix UI primitives with custom design system (glassmorphism cards, amber accent).
Animated page transitions with CSS keyframes (fade-up, scale-in).

sections.title: URL Management
items: Dashboard with full URL table: sort, search, filter, paginate.
Inline URL shortening from the landing page (anonymous).
Advanced shortening dialog with custom alias, visit limit, expiration date.
Per-row actions: copy short URL, open original, QR code modal, analytics modal.
Bulk URL creation via API keys.
CSV export of your URLs.
QR code generation (PNG, configurable size).
Link preview endpoint (Open Graph metadata: title, description, og:image).

sections.title: Authentication & Accounts
items: Registration with email/password validation.
Login with JWT token-based auth, stored in localStorage.
Password reset flow (request → email → confirm).
Account settings page with password change.
OAuth2 login with Google and GitHub (spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client).
OAuth2 users automatically created on first login; email locked to provider.
Login attempt rate limiting (20 attempts/day per IP).

sections.title: Dashboard & Analytics
items: Per-link analytics with visit count, progress bar (vs visit limit).
Dashboard stats: total URLs, total visits, active API keys.
Recent links sidebar on landing page (5 most recent).
"View all" link to full dashboard.
URL deactivation and permanent deletion with confirmation dialogs.

sections.title: API Key Management
items: Generate, revoke, and manage API keys.
API key usage tracking (calls used / limit).
Expiration dates on API keys.
X-Api-Key header support for programmatic access.

sections.title: Admin Panel
items: Admin dashboard with system stats (total URLs, users, visits, cache status, uptime).
User management: edit email, API key slots, active status.
User deletion with confirmation.
Server metrics: JVM memory, Java version, active profiles, request count.

sections.title: Backend: Performance Overhaul
items: Read-only transactions (@Transactional(readOnly = true)) at class level on all services.
Redis caching with 60-min TTL on URL peek lookups; graceful degradation on Redis outage.
Migrated from Gradle to Maven for faster builds and simpler configuration.
Java 21 + Spring Boot 3.x upgrade.
Removed unused beans, exceptions, and tests (code cleanup).
OAuth2 URL configuration via environment variables.
Default CORS configuration.

sections.title: Scheduled Tasks
items: URL expiry notifications: daily at 8 AM, emails users about URLs expiring within 24 hours.
URL deactivation: every minute, deactivates expired URLs.
API key deactivation: every hour, expires old API keys.
User deactivation: daily at 10 AM, disables unused accounts after configurable inactivity period.
IP cleanup: every minute, removes old IP address records.
Reset token cleanup: every minute, deactivates expired password reset tokens.

sections.title: Security & Compliance
items: Google Safe Browsing API v4 integration — every URL checked before shortening.
JWT stateless authentication with configurable secret and expiry.
Client IP resolver with ForwardedHeaderFilter support (works behind proxies).
Actuator endpoints: /actuator/health public, all others ROLE_ADMIN only.
CORS configured for frontend origin + standard HTTP methods.

sections.title: Infrastructure
items: Docker multi-arch builds (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64).
GitHub Actions CI: build → test → Docker push to ghcr.io on main branch.
PRs trigger build-only (no push).
Docker Compose for local development (Postgres + Redis + MailHog).
Individual Dockerfiles for flexible deployment.
Portainer environment variables for OAuth2 secrets.

sections.title: Tests
items: 140+ unit tests across controllers, services, validators, converters, and models.
JUnit 5 + Mockito + AssertJ test stack.
No Testcontainers, no @ActiveProfiles, no test slicing — all pure Mockito unit tests.

releases.summary: First public release with Angular frontend and Spring Boot backend.

sections.title: Core Features
items: URL shortening with auto-generated and custom aliases.
Visit limits (link stops working after N clicks).
Expiration dates (link expires at specific time).
Link analytics with per-URL visit tracking.
Dashboard for managing all your shortened URLs.
User registration and authentication.
Password reset via email.
API key generation and management.
QR code generation for any short URL.
Admin user management (CRUD, activate/deactivate).

sections.title: Tech Stack
items: Angular 14+ frontend with Material Design components.
Spring Boot 3.x backend with Spring Data JPA.
PostgreSQL database with Liquibase migrations.
Redis caching layer.
Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
Docker deployment on Heroku.

releases.summary: Early development phase. Core backend built out, frontend prototyped.

sections.title: Foundations
items: JPA entity model: Url, User, ApiKey, Authorities, ResetToken, IPAddress.
Spring Security with JWT authentication filter.
Liquibase changelog for schema migrations.
Codebook tables for user roles (ROLE_USER, ROLE_ADMIN).
SafeBrowsing API client (Google Safe Browsing v4).
URL validator: SafeBrowsing check, URL format, expiration date validation.
User registration with email uniqueness check, password encoding.
Password reset token flow with expiry.
Base64-encoded images in email templates.
Anonymous URL creation with duplicate detection (same longUrl returns existing).
Visit tracking with IP uniqueness (one visit per IP per URL).
Rate limiting on login attempts (Guava cache, 20/day per IP).
MailHog integration for local email testing.
Controller advice for consistent error responses.
Startup data initializer for local dev users.
